new_statements.quote: Die Betonung hängt im Ruziba nicht von der Anzahl der Silben eines Wortes oder von der Art der Bestandteile der Silbe ab, sondern lediglich von der grammatikalischen Form, in welcher das Wort oder der Satz stehen. [...] Diese Art und Weise der Betonung erschwert das Verstehen der Sprache sehr. Eine bestimmte Regel läßt sich auch für die Betonung noch nicht angeben. (ZfK 3: 4) — Die Bazinza haben keine eigene Sprache. Sie sprechen einen Dialekt des Ruziba, der hier Ruzinza heißt [...]. Die Abweichungen von dieser Grammatik sind so unbedeutend, daß man sie in Kürze in folgenden Punkten zusammenfassen kann. (ZfK 4: 257)
new_statements.translation: Accentuation in Ruziba does not depend on the number of syllables of a word or on the nature of the syllable's constituents, but solely on the grammatical form in which the word or the sentence stands. [...] This manner of accentuation makes understanding the language very difficult. No definite rule can yet be given for the accentuation either. — The Bazinza have no language of their own. They speak a dialect of Ruziba, here called Ruzinza [...]. The deviations from this grammar are so insignificant that they can be summarised briefly in the following points.
new_statements.citation: Rehse, Hermann. 1912/13. Die Sprache der Baziba in Deutsch-Ostafrika. Zeitschrift für Kolonialsprachen 3(1): 1-33, §4 Betonung, p. 4; applied to Zinza by Rehse, Hermann. 1914. Eigentümlichkeiten in der Sprache der Bazinza in Deutsch-Ostafrika. Zeitschrift für Kolonialsprachen 4: 257.
new_statements.locator: ZfK 3 (1912/13), Rehse, §4 'Betonung', p. 4 (the scanned textof the pt.1 text file); ZfK 4 (1914), Rehse, Vorwort, p. 257 (the scanned textof the pt.4 text file; PDF of pt.4 saved)

Both quoted passages are present. Differences are scanned noise only: the file reads 'Dio Bazinza haben keine eigene Sprache. Sie sprechen einen Dialekt des Ruziba, der hier Ruzinza heißt (vorgl. meine Grammatik „Die Sprache der ]}aziba..".. Die Abweichungen von dieser Grammatik sind so unbedeutend, daß man sie in Kürze in folgenden Punkten zusammenfassen kann' and 'Die Betonung hängt im Ruziba nicht von der Anzahl der Silben eines Wortes oder von der Art der Bestandteile der Sil…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Per Rehse, word accent (what he writes as an acute 'Ton') is not positional (not tied to syllable count, weight or the penult) but is determined by the grammatical form of the word; he can state no general rule, only special cases: the augment/'article' is accented (ómukazi, ómushaija), the stem syllable of underived infinitives (kutéra, kubóna), some verbal derivatives accent the stem and others the penult (kugámba vs kugambíra), and subject pronouns are accented (yámutera). Given that Haya and Zinza are tone languages (Odden 2000 'phrasal tonology'), this 'Betonung' is most plausibly grammatical tone, not stress; the source itself never says 'tone language'. Statement is for Ruziba (Haya); Rehse 1914 applies the grammar wholesale to Ruzinza.
new_statements.exceptions: Rehse says no rule can be stated and only special cases can be listed: article/augment accented; infinitive stem syllable; derivatives vary between stem and penult; subject pronouns accented; the acute marks the accented syllable throughout the grammar. Preface also mentions 'die verschiedenartige Betonung eines und desselben Wortes' and 'das fast völlige Fehlen eines Satz-Akzentes' (p. 1).
new_statements.domain_note: Word and sentence ('in welcher das Wort oder der Satz stehen'); 1912 field notes by a colonial administrator, impressionistic, no instrumental basis; the question is marked by intonation only (p. 6).
new_statements.identity_note: The only first-hand accent statement that could be opened is Rehse's 1912/13 grammar of Ruziba (= Haya, haya1250; Kiziba dialect), not of Zinza. Rehse's 1914 Zinza note (ZfK 4: 257) states that the Bazinza "have no language of their own" but speak a dialect of Ruziba called Ruzinza whose deviations from that grammar are "so insignificant" that he lists them in a few points, none concerning accent; so the Ruziba statement applies to Zinza only by Rehse's own equation of the two. Glottolog separates zinz1238 from haya1250, and Odden (2000, 2006) treats Zinza as a language in its own right with its own phrasal tonology.

sources.note: §4 'Betonung' (p. 4): accent in Ruziba depends not on syllable count or syllable make-up but solely on the grammatical form of the word/sentence; no definite rule can yet be given; special cases: the pre-prefix 'article' is stressed (ómukazi), the stem syllable of underived infinitives (kutéra), some derivatives shift 'den Ton' to the penult (kugámba > kugambíra), subject pronouns are stressed; accent marked with an acute in the grammar. Describes Haya (Kiziba), applied to Zinza only via the 1914 note.

sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. Preface (p. 257) says Zinza is a dialect of Ruziba with negligible differences (sh > s, j > d, -ai > -a, ki- ~ chi-, some lexical and women's-speech items) and refers to Rehse's Ruziba grammar (ZfK 3, 1912/13); rest is name-taboo lexicon, phrases, songs and tales. a full-text search for stress/accent Betonung/Akzent/Ton found only remarks on emphatic interjections (pp. 279, 283).
